title: The Admonishing Verse of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva
excerpt: Time passes swiftly, and human life is impermanent. Those who study the Buddha-Dharma must remain ever vigilant, and must never be careless, frolic in idle pleasures, or squander their time and end in endless regret.

inline.s: Time passes swiftly, and human life is impermanent. Those who study the Buddha-Dharma must remain ever vigilant, and must never be careless, frolic in idle pleasures, or squander their time and end in endless regret.
The Admonishing Verse of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva says:
“This day has passed
(now that today is over)
, and life decreases accordingly
(our days in this world are likewise reduced by one)
, like fish in dwindling water
(like fish in a pond whose water dries up day by day)
, what joy is there in this
(what joy can there be)
? O great assembly! Be diligent and strive
(you should practice with diligence and vigor)
, as if your head were on fire
as urgently as one would save one's own head, without a moment's delay
. Reflect on impermanence
(keep the coming of death in mind at every moment)
, and never be heedless
(never indulge yourself, craving ease and comfort while wasting precious time)
[Be diligent and strive, as if saving your burning head] You should practice with diligence and vigor,
as urgently as one would save one's own head, without a moment's delay. (For example, when something is about to strike your head, you must immediately ward it off or dodge,
not wasting a single moment
. Likewise, when death comes upon us, the practice that liberates this body must
be diligent and vigorous,
not wasting a single moment
.) The character ran is used as a word-ending suffix indicating a state, for example: xianran (obviously), huran (suddenly), piaopiaoran (driftingly).
This line means: death is rapidly approaching, and Buddha-recitation should
be diligent and unflagging,
hastily
and without delay, seizing the time before confusion and death,
to accomplish 'ten thoughts in unbroken succession, accumulated practice becoming second nature'
(for details, see
The Conditions for Rebirth

[Impermanence] Nothing abides (all dharmas in the world arise and cease, flow and change, not lasting even an instant); it also refers to death, the ghost that seizes the soul. [Never be heedless] Never indulge yourself, craving ease and comfort while wasting precious time. The Buddha said:
“Though you toil diligently for a lifetime, in an instant you will be reborn in the land of the Buddha of Infinite Life, with boundless joy.”
(The Buddha Speaks of the Buddha of Infinite Life Sutra)
